title: Event-fence reconnect grace and prioritized fragment replay
creator: Sana Patel
description: Design and implement an "event-fence" for SSE streams to enable safe reconnects without producing partially-applied structured outputs. Introduces a reconnect grace period and fragment prioritization so the server and clients can negotiate replay behavior when a connection drops mid-fragment or during function/tool-call boundaries. Goal: reduce duplicate/partial outputs and minimize client-side logic while maintaining backward compatibility with older SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits fence-id metadata for each fragment boundary and accepts fence-based resume requests
Clients can specify a reconnect grace window and receive prioritized fragment replay marked as "replay" events
No structured output (JSON/ToolCall) is delivered to the consumer in a state that would violate atomicity guarantees after a reconnect
End-to-end tests show <0.05% increase in end-user duplication and <5ms p95 latency regression on steady-state workloads
Feature gated and rolled out behind runtime-1.20 feature flag; graceful fallback for legacy clients
comments: 2026-02-16 - Sana: Posted initial design doc and prototype flow. Proposed fence-id + watermark scheme so reconnects can request a stable replay boundary.

2026-02-20 - Elena Rodriguez (Review): Prefer bounded memory window. Suggest using prioritized eviction: keep fragments that terminate a function/tool-call boundary for longer than arbitrary prose fragments.

2026-02-22 - Marcus: Added fragment prioritization prototype: priority tiers = {boundary, semantic-sentinel, body}. Boundary fragments retained 30s, semantic 10s, body 3s. Running chaos test with jittered disconnects.
